A longer story

We’ve been here before

Every generation of believers has faced a technology that felt like it might change everything. Every time, the faithful response was the same: not fear, not blind embrace. Stewardship.

1450s · The printing press

A disruptive machine became the engine of Scripture reaching millions.

1920s · Radio

Among the earliest scheduled broadcasts were worship services, reaching people who could never reach a pew.

1990s · The internet

Ministries and mission organizations were early adopters of the web.

The distrust is not paranoia.
It is memory.

34%

error rate when commercial facial recognition read the faces of dark-skinned women. For light-skinned men: 0.8%.

MIT Media Lab · Gender Shades
Wrongful arrests by machine
Bias at scale

A discernment framework

Four questions to ask of any tool

  1. 01
    Does it serve the person in front of us?

    Not the org chart, not the metrics: the actual human being.

  2. 02
    Does it protect the vulnerable?

    Their data, their dignity, their trust, especially children and people in crisis.

  3. 03
    Does it tell the truth?

    Would we gladly disclose that AI helped make this? If not, why not?

  4. 04
    Does it return time to what only humans can do?

    Presence, relationship, formation, or does it quietly replace them?

Four yeses → proceed. Any no → pause, redesign, or decline.

The real trade

AI can draft
the letter.
It cannot sit
with the grieving.

Efficiency is not the mission. Presence is. The only honest measure of these tools is what we do with the hours they return to us:

One more home visitOne unhurried conversationOne hour of real mentoring

The invitation

What your congregation can do tomorrow

01

Opt in, visibly

Use one AI assistant on real work. Explain what you checked, changed, and kept human.

02

Open your doors

Host an AI-literacy night or family workshop. Make the fellowship hall a trusted classroom.

03

Send us your builders

Connect the girl, parent, artist, athlete, or career changer to a real learning pathway.

04

Build it together

You have community trust. We have curriculum and career pathways. Together, that is infrastructure.

Nobody opts in because of a memo. People opt in because someone they trust goes first.
